title: The Listening Room
premise: Yara Almeida takes a teaching post at Marrow Creek Primary, where a class photo from 1974 shows eleven students and the current roster counts only ten. As Yara documents the school's quiet wrongness—attendance sheets that bleed ink, a supply closet that hums—they learn the town's founding families made a bargain: one child given to 'the Listener' beneath the school every harvest cycle in exchange for prosperity. The missing children aren't gone; they sit in a room below the foundations, listening, waiting for someone to return what was taken. When Yara's own grandmother is revealed as the 1974 bargain-maker who substituted an outsider's child instead of her own daughter, Yara must descend during the harvest moon and give back the stolen name—or become the twelfth listener forever.
about_author: Gideon Almeida is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in small-town classrooms before turning to horror full-time. They write at night, in a house with too many chairs.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Yara Almeida arrives in Marrow Creek and unpacks in their grandmother's drafty house, finding a framed 1974 class photo with eleven smiling faces. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hopeful new beginnings shadowed by an unexplained unease.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: On the first day, Yara's homeroom roster lists ten students, but the classroom holds eleven desks that no one claims. The janitor, Mr. Okafor, warns them not to count out loud. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness beneath mundane routine.

chapters.title: The Hum
chapters.summary: Yara hears a low hum from beneath the floorboards during silent reading; only the students seem unsurprised. A girl named Pru writes 'it likes when you listen' on a scrap of paper. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: isolation—the adults know something.

chapters.title: Grandma's Chair
chapters.summary: At home, Yara notices every recent photograph of grandma's kitchen now contains an extra wooden chair against the wall. Grandma Odette goes pale and burns the prints. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: domestic safety curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Faculty Meeting
chapters.summary: Principal Voss deflects Yara's questions about the 1974 photo with practiced charm. In the parking lot, teacher Ruth Ellery whispers: 'Ask about the harvest fund.' POV: Yara. Emotional beat: first ally, first confirmation of conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Harvest Fund
chapters.summary: Ruth explains the town's founding families endowed a 'harvest fund' in 1974—money paid annually to keep something satisfied. She refuses to say what. POV: Ruth (flashback-tinged present). Emotional beat: guilt of complicity.

chapters.title: Pru's Drawing
chapters.summary: Student Pru draws the classroom with twelve figures: ten children, Yara, and a tall shape by the door labeled THE LISTENER. Yara keeps the drawing as evidence. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: protective instinct igniting.

chapters.title: Basement Door
chapters.summary: Following the hum, Yara finds a bricked-over door beneath the gym stairs, warm to the touch. Scratched inside the mortar: eleven tally marks, freshly cut. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread made physical.

chapters.title: Odette's Silence
chapters.summary: Yara confronts Grandma Odette, who admits she attended Marrow Creek in 1974 but will not say which child was hers. That night, all the clocks in the house stop at 3:11. POV: Odette. Emotional beat: a matriarch's terror of her own past.

chapters.title: The Tenth Student
chapters.summary: Yara cross-references old records: the 1974 photo shows eleven students, but enrollment records list ten—except one name, Tomas Reyes, appears nowhere else in any archive. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: documentary obsession becoming compulsion.

chapters.title: What Okafor Knows
chapters.summary: Mr. Okafor confesses his father helped brick the basement door in 1974 after 'the taking.' Every generation, the Listener asks for a name; the town provides one. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: inherited shame.

chapters.title: Photographs Multiply
chapters.summary: The extra chair now appears in photos Yara took years ago, in other cities. It is getting closer. Pru stops coming to school. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the horror crossing thresholds it shouldn't.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Principal Voss offers Yara a generous transfer and a bonus, revealing the town has bought off teachers before. Yara refuses. That night, someone leaves a dead sparrow on their porch. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: temptation and defiance.

chapters.title: Ruth's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ruth surrenders a hidden ledger listing every name given since 1974—eleven names, each struck through except the last: blank, awaiting this year's harvest moon. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: courage at personal cost.

chapters.title: Tomas Reyes
chapters.summary: Research reveals Tomas Reyes was a migrant worker's son, enrolled for three days in October 1974 before vanishing. He was never anyone's choice—he was convenient. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: righteous anger at the town's cruelty.

chapters.title: Odette Breaks
chapters.summary: Odette finally confesses: in 1974, the lot fell to her daughter—Yara's mother. She bribed the registrar to substitute Tomas instead. The Listener noticed. It has been waiting for the debt to come home. POV: Odette. Emotional beat: devastating maternal guilt.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Pru returns changed, speaking in unison with an unseen voice, reciting names from the ledger backward. The eleventh desk is now occupied by something wearing Pru's coat. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: horror reaching the innocent.

chapters.title: Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Yara crashes the founders' council meeting and demands they return Tomas's name properly. Elder Corliss sneers: outsiders don't get votes. But two younger families abstain—a crack in the wall. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: lonely moral stand gaining fragile allies.

chapters.title: The Listening Room
chapters.summary: Okafor unlocks a maintenance hatch; Yara descends and glimpses the room below—eleven small chairs facing a wall, and a twelfth, larger, empty. Something breathes in rhythm with the hum. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: awe and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Marked
chapters.summary: Yara's own reflection now shows them seated in the twelfth chair. Their handwriting begins changing on lesson plans, slanting toward someone else's script. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: identity eroding.

chapters.title: Mother's Letters
chapters.summary: Yara finds letters from their mother, who fled Marrow Creek pregnant in 1999 and died young elsewhere—fleeing didn't save her; it just deferred the debt. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Corliss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elder Corliss privately offers Yara a deal: give the Listener Pru's name, and the town will let Yara walk away rich. Yara records the offer on their phone. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: fury crystallizing into strategy.

chapters.title: The Rules
chapters.summary: Odette recalls the ritual's terms from 1974: a name must be returned willingly, spoken over the original theft-site, before the harvest moon sets. Coerced names don't count. The Listener checks intent. POV: Odette. Emotional beat: desperate hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone steals Yara's documentation—notebooks, photos, the recording of Corliss. Only Pru's drawing survives, hidden in a library book. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: violation and resolve.

chapters.title: Allies Fracture
chapters.summary: Ruth recants under pressure from the council; Okafor disappears. Yara stands nearly alone as the harvest moon waxes full. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: cowardice and its self-loathing.

chapters.title: Okafor's Return
chapters.summary: Okafor returns bruised, having been held by the council, and brings his father's 1974 blueprint showing a second entrance to the Listening Room through the old well behind the school. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: redemption chosen late.

chapters.title: Pru Speaks
chapters.summary: In a lucid moment, Pru tells Yara the Listener doesn't want a replacement—it wants acknowledgment. Eleven children were never mourned; they were erased. Grief, freely given, might open the door. POV: Pru. Emotional beat: innocence carrying the truth.

chapters.title: Naming the Dead
chapters.summary: Yara publicly reads all eleven names at the school assembly, including Tomas Reyes, forcing the town to hear what it buried. Parents weep; Corliss storms out; the hum stops—for one full minute. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: catharsis as weapon.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: That night the school floods from below; the extra chair appears in Yara's bed. The Listener is angry—or hungry. Two days remain until the harvest moon. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the cost of truth arriving early.

chapters.title: Odette's Choice
chapters.summary: Odette prepares to offer herself in Tomas's place, arguing a willing substitution of equal weight may satisfy the debt. Yara refuses to let her. POV: Odette. Emotional beat: love versus penance.

chapters.title: The Well
chapters.summary: Yara, Okafor, and Odette reach the well at dusk on harvest eve. The rope is already frayed from the inside, as if something climbed partway up and went back down. Waiting. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: threshold terror.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Yara descends alone with Tomas Reyes's restored enrollment record and a photograph of his family. The tunnel breathes warmth. Below, eleven small voices whisper 'you came' in unison. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: sacrificial courage.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Chair
chapters.summary: In the Listening Room, the tall figure sits Yara in the twelfth chair and listens—not to words, but to Yara's memory of every document, every name read aloud. Documentation, it turns out, was prayer all along. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: revelation and surrender.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: The Listener weighs Yara's offering: Tomas's name, restored and mourned, against the town's fifty years of lies. It accepts the name—but demands the lie-givers attend. Above, the harvest moon begins to set. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: judgment suspended.

chapters.title: Climb Up, Speak Out
chapters.summary: Yara surfaces and drags the council elders, Corliss included, to the well's edge, making each speak Tomas's name and their own complicity aloud. Corliss breaks first, sobbing. The ground exhales. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: forced accountability.

chapters.title: Harvest Moonset
chapters.summary: As the moon touches the horizon, the humming swells to a chorus of eleven voices singing a skipping rhyme, then silence. The well collapses inward, sealed. The extra chair appears in one final photograph—empty, and then gone. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: release trembling on exhaustion.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Pru wakes whole with no memory of the lost weeks. The eleventh desk vanishes from the classroom. Voss resigns; the council dissolves; Ruth returns with the ledger to build a memorial wall bearing all eleven names. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: cautious repair.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Yara finishes the semester, then another. Some students still pause at the gym stairs, listening, but the sound is only pipes now. Odette plants a tree for Tomas by the playground. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief integrated, vigilance retained.

chapters.title: The Last Photograph
chapters.summary: Developing a final roll of film, Yara finds one last image: the Listening Room, empty, all twelve chairs folded and stacked neatly—as if closed for the season. On the wall, fresh chalk: THANK YOU FOR LISTENING. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: peace with a lingering shiver.

chapters.title: Enrollment
chapters.summary: Years later, Yara—still teaching, still documenting—receives an application from a new student named Reyes, transferring to Marrow Creek. Yara looks at the eleventh desk, which they kept, and smiles: some names come home to stay. Final line echoes chapter one's attendance call. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: cyclical closure, hope earned.
